title: Financial worry reaches trust and vote through a non-monotonic, identity-laden panel path
source_unit: ANES 2016-2020-2024 panel respondent retained in the 2024 panel subset

denominator.unit: valid weighted panel observations in cross-tab

observations.method: Official ANES 2024 Full Release SDA weighted descriptive cross-tab, filtered to the 2016-2020-2024 panel subset; trust categories combine some-of-the-time and never rows.
observations.uncertainty: Complex-design standard errors are reported in the source table but no formal contrast test is reproduced here; panel retention, political identity, information, and prior beliefs remain confounders.
observations.counterinterpretation: The pattern is non-monotonic and does not support a simple more-worry/less-trust law; worry is not a direct bill or price measure.

observations.period: 2024 pre-election to post-election; financial worry × reported presidential vote

denominator.unit: valid weighted panel observations in cross-tab

observations.method: Official ANES 2024 Full Release SDA weighted descriptive cross-tab, with pre-election worry and post-election reported candidate choice in the 2016-2020-2024 panel subset.
observations.uncertainty: Complex-design standard errors are reported in the source table but no formal contrast or causal model is reproduced; candidate self-report is not independently validated here and prior party identity is a major alternative explanation.
observations.subgroup: Financial-worry rows; post-election reported presidential vote.
observations.counterinterpretation: Temporal ordering does not establish that worry caused vote choice; worry, identity, retrospective judgment, information, and candidate preference may jointly shape both.

boundary: This is an official SDA descriptive ANES panel comparison, not a causal economic-voting estimate, representative full-cross-section result, direct price or hardship measure, trust mechanism, or proof that material worry produced a vote. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo because direct panel microdata download was not locally reproducible.
